note: Every entry is a transcription made by the studio. The basis field is the studio's original wording; read it with the label in the recipe: an entry without a published raw file is REPORTED, whatever its basis says.
recipe: Read the input, gate the output: two image-to-video faults from one bake-off start

receipts.claim: First two canary clips, one conditioning still
receipts.value: The conditioning still was a two-panel composite (a front three-quarter view on the left, a turned view on the right, a black divider). Both models animated it as a split-screen video; neither clip was a single-shot close-up. The reader inferred a pipeline fault (crop from a sheet), not a model fault
receipts.caveat: One AI reader, one still, one clip per model; clips not published.

receipts.value: Single full-frame close-up, no split screen. Face and accessories held; framing pulled back from 0.5 s to a waist-up medium by 1 s; the mouth was closed only at t=0 and open and talking at 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4 s and the last frame (roughly 90 percent of the clip, reader's estimate); a sleeveless jacket and an arm tattoo not in the still appeared from 1 s. Reader scores (1 to 5): identity 3, motion 4, mouth-closed 1, cleanliness 4
receipts.caveat: One reader's opinion on one clip, judged from sampled frames; not a frame count.

receipts.value: Model A: 1280x704, 24 fps, 121 frames, 5.04 s, no audio stream, hash matched the expected one. Model B: 768x512, 25 fps, 125 frames, 5.00 s, AAC audio 16 kHz mono; no expected hash, so recorded only
receipts.caveat: Read by the first reader from the files; the files are not published.

receipts.claim: Prompt changes and the mouth gate
receipts.value: Prompt changes (mouth-closed positive text, talking/open-mouth negatives, an outfit line, 2.5 to 3 s clips, 2 to 3 seeds) are untested advice. A mouth-shut gate was in build; a 30-second proof cut passed it, but 9 of its 12 shots were held closed-mouth frames used as placeholders
receipts.caveat: Does not show that the prompt changes work.

receipts.value: Model A: Apache-2.0. Model B: MIT. Both marked YES in the studio's public-use table
receipts.caveat: Read from the model cards by the studio; re-check before commercial use.

receipts.claim: What this recipe does not show
receipts.value: Repeat seeds; frame-accurate mouth-open time; other characters or lengths; audio-driven sync; speed, memory and heat; a human viewing with sound
receipts.caveat: One still, one clip per case.
